Here are a few **polished, natural-sounding options** depending on the tone Tracy wants. All keep it conversational and non-salesy.

### Warm + Professional (most balanced)
Out of curiosity, are you primarily practicing as an injector right now, or are you also involved in training or leadership within your practice?

### More Conversational
Just curious — are you mainly injecting these days, or do you also play a role in training or leading within your spa?

### Elevated / Executive
I’m curious — is your current focus strictly clinical, or are you also involved in training, mentorship, or leadership at your spa?

### Very Casual / Relationship-First
Quick question — are you mostly hands-on injecting right now, or are you involved in training or leadership on your team too?

### Slightly Strategic (good for segmentation)
Out of curiosity, do you see yourself primarily as a practicing injector today, or are you also stepping into training or leadership responsibilities at your spa?

If you want, I can tailor one specifically to Tracy’s voice (more bold, more warm, more high-end, etc.).
make thi sound better: Out of curiosity, are you currently practicing as a full-time injector or also involved in training or leadership at your spa?
turn this into a staretgy that Tracy can implent on linkedin  outreach message. thi has nothing ot do with luxora only her AIA course

Perfect. Here is a **clean, implementable LinkedIn outreach strategy for Tracy** that positions **AIA only**, using the injector-course-as-invitation angle without mentioning Luxora at all.

This is designed to feel **exclusive, educational, and relationship-first**, not salesy.

---

## Core Strategy  
**Position the AIA Injector Course as an Invite-Only Opportunity**, not a mass enrollment program.

The psychology:
People respond to **being selected**, not being pitched.

This is not:
“Buy my injector course.”

This *is*:
“We are curating the next cohort of serious injectors and educators.”

---

## Target Audiences (LinkedIn Filters)

Tracy should focus outreach to:

**Primary**
• Nurse Injectors  
• Aesthetic Nurses  
• Nurse Practitioners in aesthetics  
• Med Spa Lead Injectors  

**Secondary**
• Med Spa Owners who train internally  
• Clinical Directors  
• Injector Educators  
• Franchise Training Leads  

---

## Outreach Flow (3-Message Sequence)

### Message 1: Soft Connection Message  
Goal: Curiosity + credibility. No pitch.

**Connection Request Copy**
```
Hi [Name] — I came across your profile and love the work you’re doing in aesthetics. 
I lead Aesthetic Injector Academy and we’re currently inviting a small group of injectors into our next advanced training cohort.
Would love to connect.
```

Why this works:
• Mentions authority  
• Signals invitation  
• No ask yet  

---

### Message 2: Post-Accept Warm Message  
Send 24–48 hours after connection is accepted.

**Message Copy**
```
Thanks for connecting, [Name].

Quick context — I run Aesthetic Injector Academy and we specialize in advanced injector education that goes beyond technique into real-world confidence, consult mastery, and long-term client outcomes.

Out of curiosity, are you currently practicing as a full-time injector or also involved in training or leadership at your spa?
```

Why this works:
• Positions AIA clearly  
• Invites conversation  
• Gathers segmentation info  

---

### Message 3: Invitation Message  
Send only after they reply.

**Message Copy**
```
That’s exactly why I reached out.

We’re opening a very small, invite-only cohort of our AIA injector program and prioritizing injectors who want to elevate both their skillset and their impact within their practice.

No pressure at all — would you like me to send you details to see if it’s a fit?
```

Why this works:
• Permission-based  
• Exclusive framing  
• Zero hard sell  

---

## Optional Follow-Up (If They Don’t Respond)

Send after 5–7 days.

```
Hi [Name] — just wanted to circle back in case my note got buried.

We’re being very intentional with who we invite into our next AIA cohort, and your background stood out.
Happy to share details if it’s helpful.
```

---

## Bonus: Authority Content Tracy Should Post Weekly

To support outreach conversions, Tracy should post 2–3 short LinkedIn posts per week with angles like:

• “Why most injector courses don’t prepare you for real consults”  
• “The difference between learning technique and becoming a trusted injector”  
• “What I look for before inviting someone into AIA”  
• “Why we limit cohort size and turn people away”  

These warm the audience before the DM ever lands.

---

## What This Strategy Accomplishes

• Positions AIA as selective and premium  
• Builds inbound interest organically  
• Makes outreach feel relational, not transactional  
• Protects brand authority  
• Scales without feeling spammy  

---

If you want, next I can:
• Customize versions for owners vs injectors  
• Write Tracy’s LinkedIn profile headline to match this strategy  
• Create a 30-day LinkedIn posting calendar to support DM conversions  
• Turn this into a SOP Tracy can hand to a VA  

Just tell me how far you want to take it.

### **Med Spa & Aesthetic Acquirers / Roll-Up Platforms**
These are firms/platforms directly focused on acquiring and growing med spas:

**• Princeton Medspa Partners** – A major acquirer of medical aesthetic and cosmetic clinics. citeturn0search6  
**• MedSpa Partners (MSP)** – Leading consolidator of med spas in North America. citeturn0search14  
**• Advanced Medaesthetic Partners** – PE-backed med spa acquisition platform. citeturn0search5  
**• Alpha Aesthetics Partners** – PE-backed platform for medical spas. citeturn0search7  
**• Empower Aesthetics** (backed by Shore Capital Partners) – Emerging consolidator in aesthetics. citeturn0search5  
**• The Skin Center / Inspire Aesthetics / Ideal Image / OVME / LaserAway** – Not strictly PE firms but are large, consolidated med spa brands attractive to PE or already PE-backed. citeturn0search5  
**• AYA Medical Spa (backed by Eagle Merchant Partners)** – PE-backed med spa platform expanding via acquisitions. citeturn0search29  
**• Aviva Aesthetics** – Positioning itself as a PE-quality aesthetic platform. citeturn0search27

---

### **Private Equity Firms Actively Investing in Medical Aesthetics / Healthcare**
These firms may not be med spa “rollups” themselves but either back platforms or are active in healthcare/aesthetics:

**• Persistence Capital Partners** – Backing MedSpa Partners. citeturn0search5  
**• Princeton Equity Group** – Backs Princeton Medspa Partners. citeturn0search6  
**• Shore Capital Partners** – Backer of Empower Aesthetics. citeturn0search5  
**• Thurston Group** – Backer of Alpha Aesthetics Partners. citeturn0search5  

Other private equity firms with healthcare or broader roll-up activity (that sometimes participate directly or indirectly in med spa or healthcare roll-ups):  
**• BC Partners** – Backer of Princeton Medspa Partners. citeturn0search21  
**• VSS Capital, DuneGlass Capital, Freeman Spogli** – Reported PE firms drawing interest in med spa deals. citeturn0search10  
**• Carlyle Group, Leonard Green & Partners, Gryphon Investors** – Larger PE groups noted to deploy capital in aesthetics/related areas. citeturn0search18

---

### **Note on Market Context**
Private equity interest in med spas and medical aesthetics has increased because the industry is highly fragmented and has strong growth and recurring revenue potential. Many independent med spas are now being targeted for consolidation into larger platforms backed by private investors. citeturn0search1turn0search8

---

parts:
Bethany… I love where your brain is going with this.

But let’s zoom out strategically for a second because this could either be genius positioning or a distraction from your actual revenue engine.

You are not “just” marketing.

You are building:
• The Luxora Growth Engine  
• AI-powered acquisition + retention systems  
• Sales and revenue multiplier frameworks  
• Enterprise-level infrastructure for med spas  

So if you do an injector course, it cannot look like you’re pivoting into being “another injector trainer.”

It has to strategically support your positioning.

Here’s how I see it.

---

## Option 1: Injector Course as a Lead Magnet for Owners (Smart Play)

Instead of:
“Bethany launches injector training program”

Position it as:
**“The Business-First Injector Certification”**

Angle:
Most injector courses teach lips and tox.
Almost none teach:
• Consult conversion psychology  
• Package architecture  
• Lifetime value strategy  
• How to sell memberships  
• How to fill your book consistently  
• How to retain clients beyond one visit  

That aligns perfectly with Luxora.

This becomes:
Owner acquisition tool  
Injector retention tool  
B2B credibility asset  

You sell it to:
• Med spa owners who need team training  
• Injector academies that lack business education  
• Franchises needing standardized sales systems  

Now it’s not a marketing ploy.
It’s infrastructure.

---

## Option 2: Invite-Only Master Injector Roundtable (Higher-End Strategy)

Instead of building a full course immediately…

You host:

**Invite-Only Revenue Roundtable for Top Injectors**

Not clinical.
Business and revenue.

Topics:
• Why your book isn’t full even if you're talented  
• Why 70% of injectors are undercharging  
• How to double revenue without adding hours  
• Retention systems most spas ignore  

You film it.
You extract content.
You turn that into:
• Authority positioning  
• Podcast content  
• Paid mastermind funnel  

This is lower lift and high leverage.

---

## Option 3: Strategic JV With Tracy Olson (Most Aligned)

You already have proximity to CE-accredited education through AIA.

Instead of reinventing the wheel:

You plug Luxora into existing injector education.

Add:
“Injector Revenue Certification powered by The Luxora Collective”

Clinical + revenue + systems.

That positions you as:
The growth partner behind the scenes of injector education nationwide.

That is powerful.

---

Now let me be blunt.

If this is purely a marketing stunt to get attention…
It won’t compound.

If this becomes:
A pipeline to owners
A JV gateway
A recurring revenue asset
A credibility amplifier

Then yes.

Very smart.

---

The real question:

Are you trying to:
1. Get more med spa owner clients?
2. Expand into education licensing?
3. Increase Luxora authority?
4. Or create a new revenue stream?

Your answer changes the structure entirely.

Tell me which strategic objective this is tied to and I’ll map the cleanest execution plan.
